clue.text: Mascara I manufacture, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words should be spoken aloud and matched by sound, not spelling

parts.note: the pronoun I followed by make up, a phrasal verb meaning to manufacture or put together

explanation.surface: A cosmetics maker announces that it produces mascara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' tells you to speak 'I make up' aloud: the pronoun I sounds like the organ of sight, and the whole phrase then sounds like the name of a cosmetics category.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is one cosmetic applied around the lashes, an example of products for the face.

clue.text: Sycophant who never knows, one hears

definitions.text: Sycophant who never knows, one hears

parts.words: Sycophant who never knows, one hears
parts.note: knows sounds like noes, refusals, so the flatterer described is one who never says no to the boss

explanation.surface: A flatterer is so ignorant he never knows anything, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knows' heard aloud is 'noes', so the person never says no; 'one hears' is what signals the sound swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant always agrees with superiors, which is exactly what a compliant underling who never refuses does.

clue.text: Soft roe on for the poet

parts.note: milt is the soft roe, the sperm-filled gland of a male fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fishy food item is offered up on behalf of a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: John Milton wrote Paradise Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton is the celebrated English writer of Paradise Lost, one great verse author.

clue.text: Inflame the French, cordial at first

indicators.note: at first places the word for cordial at the front, before the French article

parts.note: cordial, meaning warm and friendly, gives kind
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Something French and friendly at the start stirs up passions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like the drink, but here it is the adjective meaning friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame is to set alight or rouse, as one would light a fire or stir feelings.

clue.text: An appeal for economy doesn't work

definitions.meaning: a plea to consume less, read as two words
describes something that fails to function, which is futile or of no help

explanation.surface: A government plea to save money proves ineffective.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it is a plea to consume less; whole, it describes something that fails to function.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea to consume less splits as two words urging thrift; whole, the word means ineffective or futile, like a thing that fails.

clue.text: A bitter draught for roving Argonauts

indicators.note: roving means wandering about, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Jason's crew on their travels are given a sour drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argonauts were Jason's crew in Greek myth; 'roving' rearranges ARGONAUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura is a brand of aromatic bitters, flavouring used in cocktails such as pink gin.

clue.text: Had a close shave

parts.note: a narrow escape described as a barber's very close trim; the phrase means left almost no margin

explanation.surface: Someone narrowly escaped disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A close shave is a narrow escape; trimming a beard very short is the literal picture behind the idiom for leaving almost no margin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving very little margin of time or space is the idiom, matching a narrow escape.

clue.text: State recalling an old trumpet call, notice

indicators.note: recalling is read as calling back, so the trumpet signal is written backwards

parts.note: a sennet is a trumpet call in Elizabethan stage directions
to notice something is to see it

explanation.surface: A US state is remembered by its old bugle call, notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalling' looks like remembering, but it means calling back, so the Elizabethan trumpet signal is read backwards before 'notice' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty United States, home of Nashville.

clue.text: Last to finish on the river

parts.note: a finish or conclusion is an end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Being the final one home along the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or survive over time, persisting.

clue.text: Worked out according to the blueprint

definitions.text: Worked out according to the blueprint

parts.words: Worked out according to the blueprint
parts.note: something that went exactly the way the drawings intended, matching the scheme

explanation.surface: A project went exactly to the design.
explanation.definitionFit: Following a blueprint means things happen exactly in line with the design or scheme.

clue.text: Still it isn't always an advancement

definitions.text: Still it isn't always an advancement

parts.words: Still it isn't always an advancement
parts.note: the opposite of keeping still is movement, but movement need not mean going forward; also a proposal put forward at a meeting

explanation.surface: Even so, progress isn't always made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'nevertheless', but it means motionless: the answer is what still is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Movement is the opposite of being still, and it can go backwards as well as forwards.

clue.text: Applied no make-up, but was brilliantly arrayed

indicators.note: make-up is read as making up, composing these letters afresh

explanation.surface: A woman wore no cosmetics yet was dazzlingly dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' looks like cosmetics, but it signals that the letters of APPLIED NO are made up anew.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoply is a full suit of armour or splendid display, so one so equipped is magnificently dressed.

clue.text: Makes a meal of taxidermy?

definitions.meaning: to cram food in greedily, gorging oneself
the craft of filling animal skins so they look alive

explanation.surface: Is the taxidermist making a fuss over his work?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes a meal of' usually means to overdo something, but here it means to eat greedily; the question mark marks the taxidermy sense as a verb from that craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorging is overeating greedily, and a taxidermist fills skins with padding; both are filling to bursting.

clue.text: One you'd hardly couple with a fast train

definitions.text: One you'd hardly couple with a fast train

parts.words: One you'd hardly couple with a fast train
parts.note: a sluggish person, pictured as a sluggish carriage that could not be hitched to an express

explanation.surface: A railway carriage unsuitable for joining to an express.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' is the railway word for joining carriages and also means to associate: you would hardly associate a dawdler with speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dawdler is a person who moves sluggishly, like an old carriage that could never keep up with an express.

clue.text: When the unimportant player comes into his own?

definitions.text: When the unimportant player comes into his own?

parts.words: When the unimportant player comes into his own?
parts.note: an extra is a minor film player, so his own period would be the extra's time, the added minutes in a match

explanation.surface: A bit-part actor's moment of glory.
explanation.walkthrough: An extra is a minor actor; the added minutes at the end of a drawn football match read as that player's own spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Added minutes after a drawn match, read as the moment belonging to a minor film actor.

clue.text: Cogent as a mixed petroleum derivative

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A persuasive argument as a blend of oil products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges COGENT AS A.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-rated fuel gas refined from crude oil, a product of petroleum.

clue.text: Forename one doesn't get in Asia

indicators.note: doesn't get in says the letter for one is left out of the continent's name

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A first name that nobody is given in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Asa is a biblical king's name and a forename.
explanation.definitionFit: Asa is a given name, as in the biblical king of Judah.

clue.text: Six-footer giving Shylock's debtor a start

indicators.note: a start means only the beginning of the merchant's name is kept

parts.note: Antonio borrows from Shylock in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice

explanation.surface: A tall man gives a moneylender's borrower a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is an insect, with six legs. Antonio is the merchant who owes Shylock a pound of flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so one tiny colony insect is literally a creature with six feet.

clue.text: Excitement caused by a love note enclosed

indicators.note: enclosed says the note sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A love letter with a note enclosed causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love note' looks like a love letter; it splits into O for love and D for a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss and bustle, a commotion, is a sense of excitement.

clue.text: Book produced by saintly figure on Latin law

indicators.note: on says the saintly figure comes after the law word in this across entry

parts.note: lex is the Latin word for law
an icon is a religious image of a saint

explanation.surface: A book written by a saint about Roman law.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary or word list is a reference volume, a kind of book.

clue.text: Grandee put out of place

indicators.note: put out of place says the letters of the nobleman are disordered

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman was displaced.
explanation.walkthrough: A grandee is a Spanish nobleman; rearranging his letters is itself the act of putting out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: To disorder or unsettle something is to throw its parts into confusion, as here.

clue.text: In addition comes to nothing

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Adding it up comes to zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Also or besides, meaning as well.

clue.text: Mainly a description not applicable to the Caspian

definitions.text: Mainly a description not applicable to the Caspian

parts.words: Mainly a description not applicable to the Caspian
parts.note: mainly puns on the main, the ocean: the Caspian is landlocked, so it is not ocean water free of land

explanation.surface: Largely, the label does not fit the Caspian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like 'mostly' but alludes to the main, the ocean; the Caspian is landlocked, so it is not ocean water out of sight of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocean water far from any coast, which a landlocked body like the Caspian cannot be.

clue.text: City turned bitterly cold

indicators.note: turned says the description is written backwards to give the city

parts.note: read as a past state, was raw: raw weather is bitterly cold

explanation.surface: A city became freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like 'became', but it is the reversal signal: 'bitterly cold' read as a description of the weather, was raw, turned around gives the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

clue.text: Banker getting the figure about right

indicators.note: about says the number goes around the letter for right

parts.note: seven is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A financier gets the sum roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' looks like a financier, but a river has banks; the Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows between banks, so in crosswords a river can be called a banker.

clue.text: Reward in coin for an Ancient Greek reporter?

definitions.text: Reward in coin for an Ancient Greek
definitions.meaning: a gold or silver piece minted in ancient Greece
one who states or declares things, a teller

explanation.surface: A Greek journalist is paid in old money.
explanation.walkthrough: The stater was an ancient Greek coin; the question mark flags the second sense, one who states.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek coin of that name, and, read literally, one who declares facts.

clue.text: The pattern of a great lawgiver

definitions.meaning: a picture made of small pieces of coloured tile or glass
relating to Moses, who gave the Israelites the Ten Commandments

explanation.surface: The design laid down by a famous lawmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Moses received the law on Mount Sinai, so things relating to him take this adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A design of inlaid tiles, and the adjective for Moses, the biblical giver of law.

clue.text: Absence without leave

parts.note: leaving one's military post without permission, abandoning duty

explanation.surface: A soldier going absent without permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning duty or one's post without permission is going absent without leave.

clue.text: Stableman lost, wandering with hesitation

indicators.note: wandering means straying about, so these letters stray into a new order

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A groom has gone astray and dithers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' rearranges LOST into OSTL.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom who looked after horses at an inn, a stable hand.

clue.text: Imperative to put in less tea, anyway

indicators.note: anyway is read as any which way, so these letters may go in any order

explanation.surface: You must cut down on the tea in any case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyway' rearranges IN LESS TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imperative is vital and necessary, required.

clue.text: Engagement for a doctor in Ulster, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the garment

parts.note: an ulster is a long heavy overcoat, so an example of a coat
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor is engaged to work in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like the province of Northern Ireland but is a long loose overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a battle or fight between forces.

clue.text: It's spliced in order to bring out the real naval spirit

definitions.text: It's spliced in order to bring out the real naval spirit

parts.words: It's spliced in order to bring out the real naval spirit
parts.note: the naval order to splice a certain rope meant issuing an extra tot of rum, the spirit

explanation.surface: A rope is joined so sailors show true naval spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splice the main brace' was the Royal Navy order for an extra rum ration; 'spirit' is the rum, not morale.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope on a sailing ship whose ceremonial splicing meant an issue of rum to the crew.
